subject: Order form — IP carveouts, output ownership and training usage
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@brighthouse.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.bell@brighthouse.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order form - IP carveouts and training use (MSA attached)

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed. We are working through the MSA + order form and legal has flagged two areas that need clearer language before Procurement can sign:

1) Output ownership / productization: BrightHome needs a clear assurance that outputs generated from our proprietary data will not be used by Redwood to productize or train commercial models without an explicit license.
2) Training / feedback license: We are proposing an opt-in model-level training permission (customer can opt-in to allow training), and a narrower feedback license limited to troubleshooting and safety improvements (no commercial re-use).

Attached is our redline (BrightHome_MSA_redlines_v1.docx) with suggested edits. Can Redwood share a concise proposal that we can run with legal? Timebox for signature would be next week if we can converge quickly.

Appreciate a point of contact on your side for legal redlines — happy to hop on a 30m call.

Best,
Alice Zhang
Head of Legal Operations
BrightHome Inc.

Attachments: BrightHome_MSA_redlines_v1.docx (document, 87 KB)
From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@brighthouse.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form - IP carveouts and training use (MSA attached)

Alice,

Thanks — got the redlines. I looped in Ben (our account lead) and Priyom (sales ops) to keep timing and procurement on track. High-level response: we can accept firm carveouts for outputs derived from customer proprietary data, and we are prepared to offer an opt-in training permission on a per-workspace basis. There are a couple of operational items we need to lock down:

- Scope language: how you define "proprietary data" vs. "publicly provided prompts" matters for enforcement.
- Auditability: we will need an evidence path (log export or artifact) showing training opt-in was applied to the workspace.
- Fallback: for the customer-protected models we propose a runtime-only variant (no model retrain) as a default.

I attached a short proposal that summarizes our suggested carveouts (redwood-proposed-carveouts.pdf). If that looks good we can hand to Laura in Legal for final mark-up. Can you confirm whether your procurement team needs a DocuSign envelope or a redline track?

Suggested next step: 30m touch with legal and procurement tomorrow (Thu). Proposed attendees: Alice, Marcus, me, Ben, and Laura Bennett (Redwood Legal). Is 11am PT OK?

Cheers,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-carveouts.pdf (PDF, 34 KB)
From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@brighthouse.com>, grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 15:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form - IP carveouts and training use (MSA attached)

Hi Alice / Grace team,

Thanks for sending the redline and the summary. I reviewed BrightHome_MSA_redlines_v1 and Grace's proposal. To keep the language operationally enforceable and concise, my recommended approach is:

1) Output ownership clause (proposed language):
   - "Customer retains title to Customer Data and to Outputs that are a deterministic transformation of Customer Data. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, exclusive license to Outputs for Customer's internal and commercial use, except where Customer explicitly licenses Output to Redwood under a separate agreement."

2) Training / feedback: two-tier model
   - Opt-in training: Customer may elect in writing to permit Redwood to use Customer Data and Outputs to fine-tune internal models; such permission will be scoped to specific model families and time windows, and documented in the Order Form.
   - Narrow feedback license: Redwood may use de-identified telemetry and aggregated feedback for safety, performance and compliance purposes only; Redwood will not use such feedback to train commercial models without explicit opt-in.

3) Operational assurances:
   - Audit logs export: Redwood will provide an audit log extract proving training opt-in events for the relevant workspace and model ID for the prior 24 months upon Customer request (subject to redaction for other customers).
   - Segregated runtime path: We will implement a runtime-only serving path for opt-out customers (no model retrain pipelines connected).

I've attached a marked-up MSA (redwood-legal-markup-msav2.docx) with tracked changes for the clauses above. There are two optional concessions we could offer to unblock procurement quickly: (a) a 12-month rolling data-retention cap for training artifacts, or (b) an escrow arrangement for Outputs if BrightHome requests additional indemnities.

Happy to discuss on the call. If procurement wants non-US law or specific export controls called out, flag that and we'll iterate.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-legal-markup-msav2.docx (document, 48 KB)
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@brighthouse.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.bell@brighthouse.com, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form - IP carveouts and training use (MSA attached)

Laura / Grace,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the marked-up MSA. The language you propose is generally aligned with BrightHome's position. A few clarifications from Procurement/Legal before we route to our Execs for sign-off:

- Exclusive license ask: We prefer "exclusive" for Outputs tied to proprietary datasets that materially differentiate our product. If Redwood cannot accept exclusivity in all cases, we can accept an "exclusive for X months" approach or a carveout limited to narrowly defined Output classes. Please propose a duration or a restrictive scope.

- Audit logs: the exportability requirement sounds good — please confirm data format (CSV/JSON), fields included (model ID, workspace ID, timestamp, opt-in flag), and SLAs for producing the extract (e.g., 10 business days).

- Opt-in UI/contract mechanism: We prefer opt-in to be a) in the Order Form and b) supported by an API flag so our engineers can programmatically assert the workspace opt-in state. Is there an API you can expose?

Open to the two concessions you mentioned; escrow would be a heavier lift for both sides, so would prefer a 12-month rolling cap on training artifacts as a starting point.

If possible, let's lock language this week. We can do a 30m call tomorrow at 11am PT (we confirmed with Marcus).

Best,
Alice Zhang
Head of Legal Operations
BrightHome Inc.
